name: Chorotega
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog: retired bookkeeping languoid — 'There was no separate Chorotega language' (speakers were Mangue); no stress description exists for it

new_statements.quote: Todas las lenguas otomangues habladas hoy en día son tonales (Campbell, 2007a, p. 7; Hernández, 2021, p. 1), probablemente como resultado de la existencia de tonos contrastivos en el proto-otomangue. Por esta razón, es muy factible que el mangue también tuviera tonos léxicos, aunque en ninguna de las fuentes aparece información precisa acerca de rasgos suprasegmentales. [...] Por su cercanía genealógica con el chiapaneco y los varios conjuntos de palabras homógrafas que se hallan en las transcripciones, también se puede sostener que el mangue contaba con tonos contrastivos, pero el número exacto y la naturaleza de cada uno son imposibles de determinar.
new_statements.translation: All Otomanguean languages spoken today are tonal ..., probably as a result of contrastive tones in Proto-Otomanguean. For this reason it is very plausible that Mangue also had lexical tones, although none of the sources contains precise information about suprasegmental features. [...] Given its close genealogical relationship to Chiapanec and the several sets of homographic words found in the transcriptions, it can also be maintained that Mangue had contrastive tones, but the exact number and the nature of each are impossible to determine. (Quirós 2002 p. 66, same verdict: 'Neither the condition of the language -extinct- nor the quality of the materials consulted allow one even to venture a hypothesis about the suprasegmentals. Possibly, and because other languages of the family have them, Mangue had tone and quantity.')
new_statements.citation: Krohn, Haakon S. 2022. Fonología del mangue (chorotega). Káñina, Rev. Artes y Letras, Univ. de Costa Rica 46(3): 7-29. doi:10.15517/rk.v46i3.52228 (corroborated by Quirós Rodríguez 2002, Diccionario español-chorotega, chorotega-español, EUCR, 'Fonemas suprasegmentales', p. 66)
new_statements.locator: Krohn 2022, sec. 5 'Suprasegmentales', pp. 24-25 (and Conclusiones p. 25); Quirós 2002 p. 66
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: QUOTE CHECK. Opened (text layer of the saved PDF; Krohn 2022, Kanina 46(3): 7-29, CC BY-NC-ND open access per the saved UCR landing page). Section '5. Suprasegmentales' begins at text line 1038 (printed p. 24) and runs onto p. 25. Both halves of the reported quote are there word for word: 'Todas las lenguas otomangues habladas hoy en dia son tonales (Campbell, 2007a, p. 7; Hernandez, 2021, p. 1), probablemente como resultado de la existencia de tonos contrastivos en el proto-otomangue. Por esta razon, es muy factible que el mangue tambien tuviera tonos lexicos, aunque en ninguna de las fuentes aparece informacion precisa acerca de rasgos suprasegmentales.'... [Albornoz acento largo/breve fo…
new_statements.rule_in_words: No rule: the language is extinct and recorded only in untrained 19th-century transcriptions; both modern analysts state that nothing can be said about suprasegmentals beyond a comparative inference that Mangue was probably tonal (Quirós: tone and quantity). Brinton 1886 p. 244 notes only that his sources mark an acute accent which 'appears to be syllabic'. No statement anywhere on where word stress falls.
new_statements.exceptions: None; Brinton 1886 cites Albornoz's Chiapanec minimal pair nolō 'snake' / nolô 'flower' as evidence that 'accent' (prosody) was distinctive in Chiapanec-Mangue, without locating it.
new_statements.domain_note: Not applicable; the only prosodic evidence is sporadic acute marks on isolated citation forms in Rocha 1842 / Berendt 1874 / Brinton 1886 wordlists.
new_statements.identity_note: chor1275 is a Glottolog Bookkeeping languoid: ISO 639-3 change request 2009-035 retired [cjr] ('There was no separate Chorotega language. The Chorotega Indians were speakers of Mangue'), merged into Mangue [mom] = Glottolog moni1237. Every linguistic record (Rocha 1842, Squier 1852, Berendt 1874, Brinton 1886, Lehmann 1920; Quirós 1984-2002; Krohn 2022) is Mangue of the Masaya district, Nicaragua; the Costa Rican (Nicoya) Chorotega left only a few words in Oviedo. Any catalog entry belongs under moni1237, not chor1275 (retired code confers no separate identity). A parallel audit folder for moni1237 already exists at

sources.note: Sec. 5 'Suprasegmentales' (p. 24-25): no source gives precise information on suprasegmental features; argues from Otomanguean comparanda and homograph sets that Mangue had contrastive tones whose number/nature cannot be determined; quotes Brinton 1886 on 'accent'; no statement on stress placement.

sources.citation: Quirós Rodríguez, Juan Santiago. 1985. Observaciones sobre la tipología de la lengua chorotega o mangue. Revista de Filología y Lingüística de la UCR 11(2): 93-98. doi:10.15517/rfl.v11i2.16696
sources.note: p. 93: the fragmentary materials 'no permite en lo absoluto ser exhaustivo (no se puede, por ejemplo, decir nada sobre los suprasegmentales ni sobre la oración compuesta)'.

sources.citation: Berendt, C. Hermann. 1874. Lengua chorotega o mangue (diria de Squier) et lengua maribia de subtiaba (nagrandan de Squier). Ms., Nicaragua 1874. University of Pennsylvania Ms. Coll. 700, Item 144 (31 openings; comparative vocabulary Chiapanec / Mangue of Masaya, Masatepe, Niquinohomo, Namotivá / Subtiaba).
sources.note: Pure tabular vocabulary (c. 750 words, numerals, 81 phrases) plus a pasted-in Correspondenz-Blatt (Sept. 1874) ethnographic notice; no orthographic or prosodic remarks.

sources.citation: Brinton, Daniel G. 1886. Notes on the Mangue; an extinct dialect formerly spoken in Nicaragua. Proceedings of the American Philosophical Society 23(122): 238-257.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online
sources.note: p. 244 ('Phonetics'): 'Accent is of the utmost importance in both these dialects [Mangue and Chiapanec]... Albornoz gives this very example to illustrate the importance of accent, nolō, a snake, nolô, a flower. Unfortunately, none of my authorities employ any accentual mark but the acute, and this appears to be syllabic.' No placement rule.

sources.citation: Quirós Rodríguez, Juan Santiago. 1988. El sistema vocálico de la lengua chorotega o mangue. Revista de Filología y Lingüística de la UCR 14(2): 129-132. doi:10.15517/rfl.v14i2.18975
sources.note: Vowels only; vowel vacillations attributed possibly to untranscribed conditioning factors 'posiblemente, de carácter suprasegmental'; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Squier, E. G. 1852. Nicaragua; its people, scenery, monuments, and the proposed interoceanic canal. Vol. 2. New York: D. Appleton. (pp. ~310-323: aboriginal languages, comparative vocabulary incl. 'Chorotegan, or Dirian')
sources.note: 'Of what I have called Chorotegan, or Dirian, I was only able to procure the vocabulary'; the grammatical remarks concern Nagrandan (Subtiaba); nothing on accent.

sources.citation: Rocha, Juan Eligio de la. 1842 [copy by C. H. Berendt, Granada 1874]. Apuntamientos de la lengua mangue. University of Pennsylvania Ms. Coll. 700, item 140 (6 leaves). FAMSI Mesoamerican Language Texts Digitization Project.
sources.note: Wordlist, numerals and phrases only; no prose on pronunciation. A few forms carry an acute accent (píndih, Cumbú, rumú, Nejá, Cejó, rismóh, zumú, múta, pumé) with no explanation.
